title: Operator notebook: compact metrics & span lab notes
content:
Purpose: quick operator-facing reference that condenses the most useful, low-noise signals for fast incident triage on multi-tenant inference.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: oncall engineers, SREs, and onshift platform engineers who must find root cause quickly with minimal dashboard real estate.
- Scope: a compact metric index (3–7 fields per metric), a minimal set of tracing span anchors, and a recommended micro-dashboard layout plus short investigation steps.

Design principles (brief):
- Prefer low-cardinality aggregates by default; provide drilldown links for tenants and model ids.
- Keep panels <30s query runtime at 1m resolution; use pre-aggregated rollups for 1h+ windows.
- Instrument only what changes troubleshooting behavior; avoid per-request blowup for non-critical tags.
- Correlate top metrics with an anchor span id (trace_id) for quick trace capture.

Compact metric index (column format: name | calc | primary tag(s) | cardinality | alert guidance | why it helps):
1) server_request_qps
   - calc: sum(request_count) / 60s
   - tags: region, pool
   - cardinality: low
   - alert: sustained drop >40% for 5m (SEV2)
   - why: fast indicator of routing or front-end throttling

2) token_emit_rate
   - calc: sum(tokens_emitted) / minute
   - tags: model_family, tenant_tier
   - cardinality: medium (group by model_family when large)
   - alert: token rate drop >50% for 3m with concurrent request_count steady
   - why: distinguishes serving pause vs client-side slowdown

3) median_generation_latency_ms
   - calc: p50(generation_latency_ms)
   - tags: model_variant
   - cardinality: low
   - alert: p50 increase >2x baseline for 10m
   - why: primary latency SLI; faster to evaluate than p95 in noisy tails

4) kv_cache_hit_ratio
   - calc: hits / (hits + misses)
   - tags: model_id, tenant
   - cardinality: medium
   - alert: drop below 0.6 for 15m if prior baseline >0.8
   - why: caching regressions significantly increase cost/latency

5) batch_size_effective
   - calc: avg(tokens_per_batch)
   - tags: pool, model_family
   - cardinality: low
   - alert: sudden drop >30% indicates batching regression
   - why: impacts throughput and per-token cost

6) fallback_rate
   - calc: sum(fallbacks) / sum(requests)
   - tags: route, region
   - cardinality: low
   - alert: >1% sustained (configurable by tenant)
   - why: indicates routing or capacity fallback behavior

7) error_total_4xx_5xx
   - calc: sum(errors{status=4xx|5xx})
   - tags: error_class, model_id
   - cardinality: medium
   - alert: absolute increases (e.g., +200% over 10m) and spike in 5xx
   - why: obvious failure signal to begin trace capture

Tracing span anchors (short list of spans to capture and fields to attach):
- span: http.request.receive
  - attach: request_id, tenant_id, route, trace_id
  - notes: capture headers needed for auth debugging; short sampling rate 100% for errors
- span: model.runner.generate
  - attach: model_variant, kv_cache_hit, batch_size_effective, seq_len
  - notes: annotate with kernel selection hint if available
- span: cache.kv.lookup
  - attach: key_namespace, hit/miss, backend_latency_ms
  - notes: high-cardinality key avoided; record namespace only
- span: routing.fallback
  - attach: fallback_kind, src_region, dest_pool
  - notes: capture capacity tier and policy matched

Sampling guidance:
- Default: 0.5% for steady-state traffic across all requests (keeps trace volume low).
- Error override: 100% for any 5xx or fallback events tagged at http.request.receive.
- Session sampling: for tenant-affecting regressions, temporarily raise to 5% for 30m by feature flag.
- Retention/ingest: truncate event payloads, strip PII fields before ingest to tracing backend.

Dashboard compact layout (single row microdash idea for 6 panels):
1) small sparkline: server_request_qps (1h)
2) heatmap: median_generation_latency_ms (by model_family x region) (15m)
3) metric: kv_cache_hit_ratio current + delta (5m vs 30m)
4) gauge: batch_size_effective + histogram link
5) table: top 10 tenants by token_emit_rate change (with quick links to traces)
6) list: recent error_total_4xx_5xx spikes with linked trace ids

Panel design notes:
- Each panel must have a small link that pre-filters trace explorer with trace_id or tenant_id.
- Use compact color palette: green/amber/red for deviations above 20%/50%/200% of baseline.
- Provide a per-panel query budget label (approx query cost) to discourage expensive ad-hoc queries.

Investigation quick-runbook (3–7 minute flow):
- Step 0: glance at server_request_qps and token_emit_rate to determine user traffic vs server slowdown.
- Step 1: if token_emit_rate is low but requests normal -> client/backoff or upstream latency. Check ingress logs.
- Step 2: if requests high but kv_cache_hit_ratio dropped -> suspect cache TTL/invalidations or keying bug. Open cache.kv.lookup traces.
- Step 3: if median_generation_latency_ms high -> open model.runner.generate traces; check kernel selection and batch_size_effective.
- Step 4: if fallback_rate > threshold -> routing.fallback traces, confirm capacity policy and pool health.
- Step 5: collect 3 sample traces (error, slow, normal) and attach to incident ticket; set temporary sampling bump if needed.

Operational constraints & cost controls:
- Traces per minute target: keep <8k traces/min across all clusters; cap sampling and raise error overrides.
- For heavy tenants, use tenant-sampled aggregates (no full traces) unless authorized.
- Dashboard retention: 90 days for aggregated metrics, 7 days for raw high-cardinality drilldowns.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: How to attach kernel metadata (quantization, kernel name) to spans without exploding cardinality? Proposal: record kernel_name only for traces where generation_latency_ms > baseline*2.
- Q: Paging UX for trace links in the microdash; who owns quicklink component? Assign to UI infra team (PR sent: github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/312).
- TODO: add snippet to SDK that emits batch_size_effective and kv_cache signals with minimal overhead (owner: Marco, ETA 2026-02-01).
- TODO: create a low-cost synthetic probe that validates kv_cache_hit_ratio per model_family every 10m (owner: Priya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact: aim to reduce cognitive load during incidents. If we need more dimensions, prefer separate drilldown pages rather than enlarging the primary microdash.
- Please reply with minimum viable thresholds for alerts per region (I started with conservative defaults but we need product/tenant input).

Appendix: Useful queries (examples, adapt to backend):
- q1: rate(sum(request_count[1m])) by (region, pool)
- q2: avg_over_time(generation_latency_ms[5m]) by (model_family)
- q3: sum(kv_hits) / sum(kv_hits + kv_misses) by (model_id)
- q4: topk(10, increase(tokens_emitted[5m])) by (tenant_id)

End of notebook.
